  **What the PR does**
  - **`telemetry.py`.**
    - One `_sending` lock is held across the swap and the posts in `flush`, so a flush returns only after any send already in flight has posted.
    - Emitters never take that lock, and `_take` no longer flushes inline.
    - The post keeps the collector client's `TIMEOUT_S`. `flush` returns `Unsent("send_in_flight")` after waiting `SEND_WAIT_S` (3 × TIMEOUT_S), or `Unsent("timeout")` when its own post timed out.
    - The unused `clock` parameter is removed.
  - **`qmx-apps/tests/test_apps.py`.** The deep home is fixed at 144 characters (`DEEP_HOME`), as above.

##### ASSISTANT 2026-10-24T19:00
Good instinct to question it. But yes, it's a local address, and for a desktop app that's the right choice, both for security and professionally.

**What it is:** `127.0.0.1` means "this same computer". Nothing outside your PC can reach it, not the internet and not your home network. `47613` is just the door number QMX's little receiver listens on, and only for the few seconds of a sign-in.

**Why it's the safe choice:**
- The sign-in code never leaves your PC on the way back from cTrader. It goes from cTrader, to your browser, to your own PC, and then straight to your server.
- That code expires in about a minute and works once.
- On its own, the code is useless. Turning it into a sign-in needs your app's secret, and that lives sealed on the server.
- If another program is already holding that door, QMX refuses to start the sign-in rather than share it.

**Why a "proper" web address would be worse:** a public address like `qmx.yourdomain.com/callback` means running a web server open to the internet, with a domain, security certificates and patching. Your sign-in code would then travel to an internet-facing machine. That's more to attack and more to maintain, for no gain.

**The professional standard:** this is the documented best practice for desktop apps signing in with OAuth, in the standard called RFC 8252, "OAuth for Native Apps". It recommends exactly this local, loopback address. The GitHub and Google Cloud command-line tools and many desktop apps sign in the same way.

**When a real web address would make sense:** only if QMX ever signs in users who aren't on their own computer, like a hosted web version for other people. That's not your setup, and adding it later is just one more redirect line on the same app.

So I'd keep it as is.

Nothing is committed and no code was changed. I did the work directly, without the background agent the research skill asks for, because your brief said no sub-agents.
  
  **Patterns to adopt**
  - **The PC copy is the main copy.** Servers act as "cloud peers" for backup, as a bridge to outside services, and for extra computing, "not the source of truth" (Ink & Switch, `inkandswitch-local-first.md`). This matches rulings 136-139.
  - **One data folder kept apart from the program, picked during setup.** Zotero (Data Directory Location), Obsidian and Logseq (any folder), Anki (`-b`), Chrome (`--user-data-dir`) and VS Code portable all do this. Firefox: "you can uninstall Firefox without losing your personal information."
  - **Microsoft says app data must not hold user data:** "If the app is removed, all of the app data will be lost... Don't use app data to store... anything that users might perceive as valuable" (`ms-store-and-retrieve-app-data.md`).
  - **There is a trap on Windows today.** Velopack, the successor to Squirrel, deletes "the whole `%LocalAppData%\{packId}` folder" when you uninstall (`velopack-uninstalling.md`). MSIX also removes whatever the app wrote into AppData. QMX already writes its daemon data to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\QMX\qma-daemon` (`root.py:35-57`). Other parts use `~/.qmx`, and Hindsight's database sits in `~\.pg0`. So the installer's packId must never be `QMX`.
  - **Other patterns:** a small pointer file that says where the data folder is, rebuildable indexes left out of backups, export to open formats, and never live-syncing the live folder (Anki and Obsidian both warn against it).
  
  **Folder layout**
  - **Windows:** the data folder is `%USERPROFILE%\QMX`, or a folder he picks such as `D:\QMX`. The pointer goes in `%APPDATA%\QMX\home.toml`, state and cache in folders named `QMX-state` and `QMX-cache`, and keys stay in Credential Manager.
  - **Linux:** the data folder is `~/QMX` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/qmx`. Config, state, cache and runtime go in the matching XDG folders, following the XDG spec v0.8.
  - **macOS:** the data folder is `~/QMX` only if he chooses it in setup, otherwise `~/Library/Application Support/QMX`. Apple bars apps from writing to the user's own folders "unless explicitly directed". Caches go in `~/Library/Caches/QMX`.
  - **What goes where:** anything whose loss would cost him work goes in the data folder (Library, catalog, Parquet, memory, ledger, settings, backups). Anything QMX can rebuild goes in state or cache. Config holds only the location of the data folder.
  
  **Versioning rule**
  - A manifest at the folder root, `qmx-home.toml`, records a MAJOR.MINOR format version for the folder and for each store. SQLite files also set `application_id` and `user_version`.
  - Same major version: open normally. Unknown optional fields are ignored, the way Parquet skips page types it does not know.
  - Older major version: back up first, then migrate forward one step at a time. Zotero does this with its `zotero.sqlite.[num].bak` upgrade backups.
  - Newer major version: refuse by name and say which QMX version is needed. Firefox does this with `compatibility.ini` and `--allow-downgrade`, and Anki requires a deliberate "Downgrade" step.
  - Long-lasting formats: SQLite ("supporting SQLite until 2050", and a Library of Congress preferred format), Parquet (open spec, versioned metadata), JSON, Markdown and plain folders.
  
  **Local backup rule**
  - Snapshot the stores that cannot be rebuilt (the catalog via `VACUUM INTO`, the ledger, refs, settings, a memory dump). Copy blobs incrementally, since they never change once written.
  - Thin old copies the way Anki does: keep everything for 2 days, then a set number of daily, weekly and monthly copies.
  - Always back up before a migration, an import or a restore.
  - Keep two copies: one in the data folder's `backups/` for quick undo, and one on a second drive he chooses.
  - Restore from the launcher, with server copying paused until he confirms.
  - Anki says local backups will not survive a broken device, Zotero says sync is no substitute, and Obsidian says "Syncing is not a backup."
  
  **Do OpenObserve and Hindsight run locally on Windows?**
  - **OpenObserve: yes.** The docs give a Windows tab that runs `openobserve.exe`, though they ask for an Administrator prompt. Release v1.1.2 ships `openobserve-ee-v1.1.2-windows-amd64.zip`, about 167 MiB, with no published checksum. Single-node mode on SQLite and local disk is the default. No minimum RAM is documented. Several defaults must be changed:
    - `ZO_DATA_DIR` defaults to `./data` in the working directory, which would scatter files;
    - memory tables can use up to 50% of RAM;
    - the disk cache can use up to 50% of free disk;
    - retention is 10 years and telemetry is on;
    - it should bind to 127.0.0.1.
  - **OpenTelemetry Collector:** the Windows MSI installs a service; the tarball gives a plain executable QMX can run itself.
  - **Hindsight: yes.** Windows is "Fully supported" and works with its embedded database pg0 "out of the box". The docs call pg0 "not recommended for production". The full install needs 1.5-2 GB of RAM, plus 0.5-1 GB for Postgres. pg0 ships a Windows binary with PostgreSQL 18 and pgvector 0.8.5. pg0 can put its data in any folder, but Hindsight's own wrapper never passes that setting, so the database stays in `~\.pg0`. To keep memory inside the QMX folder, QMX should start pg0 itself with the data in `<home>/memory/pg` and point Hindsight at it through `HINDSIGHT_API_DATABASE_URL`.
  
  **Run here or there:** Docker contexts are named targets with a default and a per-command override. VS Code Remote installs a server on the remote machine, Jupyter has a kernel picker plus a server URL, and Ollama keeps one API with the address set by `OLLAMA_HOST`. For QMX: "This PC" is the default target, each server is a named target, and each job gets a "Run on" choice. The ledger records where each job ran.
  
  **Still open:**
  - Whether pg0 bundles `pg_dump`, which the memory backup step needs.
  - OpenObserve's real RAM use on the PC, still unmeasured.
  - The installer's packId.

  **Versions**
  
  `qmx-home.toml` holds the folder's format version (2) and a home id. For each store it records a version and a `min_reader` (the oldest version that can still read and write it). For SQLite stores the file itself is the truth. On open, each store follows one rule:
  - Same version: open.
  - Older: take a snapshot, then migrate forward one step at a time.
  - Newer, but this release meets `min_reader`: open normally and keep unknown fields and settings keys untouched.
  - Newer, and this release does not meet `min_reader`: refuse by name, saying which version is needed. The Library and price data open read-only instead.
  
  Indexes never refuse; they rebuild. Changes that alter what existing data means ship over two releases, so the previous release always opens the folder.

  - **Quick undo:** in `backups/` every hour, and before every migration, import, restore or folder move.

  - **Rotation:** 48 hours hourly, then 7 daily; on the second drive 14 daily, 8 weekly, 12 monthly.
  - **Restore:** a button on the start screen that works even when the folder won't open. Copying to servers stays paused until he confirms.
  - **Keys:** an optional sealed copy that his passphrase opens. A monthly restore drill runs on its own.

  No probe disproved a design fact.
  
  **What it does.** Every QMX program now finds his QMX folder one way, and none makes a folder he did not ask for.
  - There is a new stdlib-only leaf package, `D:/QMX-worktrees/bld-lf1/qmx-agents/packages/qmx-home/`. Its interface is `resolve(flag=None, *, create=False, drives=None) -> Layout`, plus `Layout`, `Label`, `NoQmxFolder`, `pointer_file()` and `LABEL`.
  - The resolver follows A2's order: flag, `QMX_HOME`, the per-OS pointer, A1's default holding a label, then each fixed drive's `QMX` holding a label.
  - The flag and `QMX_HOME` must name a folder that exists. A pointer to a missing folder is skipped, so a lost pointer reaches the drive scan.
  - Only `create=True` with a flag makes a folder. It writes a format 1 label, and only into a folder that is missing or empty, so an existing flat home is never relabelled.

The refusals `pc_not_home`, `not_paired` and `waiting_for_server` no longer apply to a PC home. `waiting_for_server` and `not_paired` stay for a home on a place. New refusal `pc_is_home`: a host that is not This PC is asked to sign in a PC-homed app.
  - `HomeSignIn` is split into two layers:
    - `open` and `exchange` run in process.
    - `begin` and `code` are the host-pass routes, and they call `open` and `exchange`.
  - `PcSignIn` takes `here`, this host's `HomeSignIn`:
    - With a local home, This PC runs the begin, the receiver and the code exchange itself, with no pairing key and no server.
    - With a place as home, it asks the place with a host pass. After the place's sign-in succeeds, `here.keys.delete("qmx/token/ctrader-app")` runs. A refused sign-in keeps This PC's pair.

    - The existing `HomeKeyStore` file serves a server.

  - A broker read on This PC opens its cTrader session with the app half from `qmx/read/ctrader-app` and the access token from Credential Manager. A row homed on a place opens no session on This PC.

It is one commit on 19d3df23: 2 files changed, 244 insertions, 30 deletions. PR 210 has a "Third review fix" line. Nothing was rebased, force-pushed or deleted.
  
  **The fix.** File: `qmx-home/src/qmx_home/__init__.py`.
  - **Blocker: a part of a QMX folder.** `resolve` and `step_to_tree` now walk up from the folder they are given. If any ancestor holds a `qmx-home.toml` label, they refuse untouched with "<x> is inside the QMX folder <ancestor>; pass <ancestor>". The step adds "; nothing in it was moved".
    - `resolve` checks this before `--create`, so it writes nothing inside a QMX folder either.
  - **Low 1: no profile folder.** When `Path.home()` raises, only the profile check is skipped. The other checks still apply.
  - **Low 2: a resumed `layout-step.json` must stay inside the folder.** I went further than "no absolute path, no `..`, under root". Every row must be a move the step itself writes: an A5 row, the host log, or one top-level name moved into `data/`.
    - So a foreign plan cannot name an absolute path, a drive, `..` or a backslash, cannot write into `keys/`, and cannot touch the label.
    - Any other row ends in LayoutRefused and nothing moves.
  - **One gate.** `resolve` and the step now share one refusal function. So `resolve` can no longer print the layout command for a folder the step would refuse, or the other way round.
  
  **Other routes to a move I found and closed (item 4).**
  1. **A foreign `layout-step.json` was enough to mark a folder as a QMX home**, because the journal counted as a marker on its own.
     - Now a folder counts as a flat home only if a real marker is at its top, or where a stopped step put it (`data/<marker>`, or `keys/control-token`). The plan file alone no longer counts.
     - A fresh folder whose labelling stopped (only empty parts plus the plan) still finishes, and that now has a test.
     - With no plan, a folder that already holds `data/` is still refused by the existing "already holds data" check.
  2. **A foreign plan could rename anything inside the folder** in any shape, including into `keys/` or onto the label. Closed by the row rule above.
  3. **A flat home holding a labelled QMX folder at its top would have moved that folder into `data/`.** This happens if he put the new folder inside his old `~/.qmx`. It is now refused by name: "holds the QMX folder <x> ... move it out first". I check only the top level, because a deeper search would walk 10,000 Library objects.
  4. **Markers now need the right kind of entry.** `claude-relayed` must be a folder and the four file markers must be files. A folder named `control.db` no longer counts.
  
  **A bug the tests caught in my first version.** My first row rule rejected a flat home's own `logs/` moving to `data/logs`. That broke resuming a real stopped step. There is now one `TAKEN` set (data, keys, backups, cache) shared by the plan builder and the plan reader.
  
  **Routes I checked and left open, none of which moves files wrongly.**
  - **A copy of `data/` outside any QMX folder** still lays out as a flat home. That copy has the old home's shape, so wrapping it in a tree is correct and takes nothing away.
  - **`qmx-recover repair` runs `chown -R` on `QMX_FOLDER` before the layout step** can refuse it. It changes owners, not locations, and the behaviour predates LF2.

  - Make a new QMX folder.
  - Open an existing QMX folder.
  - Restore, a placeholder that answers 501 until LF8.
  - Bring in the old data. This is offered and chosen first when `~/.qmx` passes LF2's gate.
  
  The choices exist as routes under `/api/first-start`, served alone on the loopback by `python -m qmx_host first-start --serve`. They also exist as commands: `first-start`, `new`, `open`, `bring-in [--old]` and `restore`, all taking `--home <target>`. Only a finished choice writes the pointer.
  
  **The never places of A1.** These targets are refused by name: inside AppData (Roaming or Local), inside QMX's own environment or checkout, a network drive or share, a drive's root, and any sync root. Sync roots come from:
  - OneDrive's `OneDrive*` variables.
  - Dropbox's `info.json`.
  - Google Drive's `DefaultMountPoint`.
  - Every root registered under `SyncRootManager`, read only. On this PC that finds OneDrive. `D:\QMX` passes.
  
  A removable drive gets a warning.
  
  **The bring-in.** It is in `qmx-agents/packages/qmx-host/src/qmx_host/bring_in.py`, and runs in order:
  1. It refuses before writing anything if:
     - LF2's gate refuses the old folder.
     - A host still serves the old folder. This is read from its process record only; no lock is taken there.
     - The target is in a never place.
     - The target and the old folder overlap.
     - Some files are kept online only.
     - There is too little room: the copy, plus twice the old Library for the switch, must leave LF3's 1 GiB floor free.
  2. It takes the per-user first-start lock (beside the pointer) and the new folder's host lock.
  3. It writes `data/migration/bring-in-unfinished.txt`.
  4. It lists and sha256-hashes every file into `data/migration/old-layout-list.json`.
  5. It copies byte for byte into the tree, using the layout step's own rows (`FLAT_TO_TREE`, `HOST_LOG`).
  6. It lists and hashes the old folder again, then rehashes every copy from disk.
  7. It runs `switch_over` on the copy only, then `check_open`.
  8. It writes `bring-in-report.json` and `bring-in-report.txt`, removes the unfinished marker, and writes the pointer.
  
  Links are listed but never followed or copied. A rerun into a finished folder returns the saved report. A second bring-in of the same old folder into another folder is refused.
  
  **Refusal in `qmx-agents/packages/qmx-control/src/qmx_control/library.py`.** `old_library(home)` refuses two cases by name, naming the bring-in command:
  - A home holding `library.db` beside an empty `library/`.
  - A home whose bring-in did not finish.
  
  `open_store` raises it. `python -m qmx_host serve|start` exits 2 with it before anything opens. A host given an unlabelled old folder now names the first start instead of the resolver's layout-step line.
  
  **Switch script.** `scripts/data/switch_library.py` now runs only on the `data/` of a QMX folder. Its `~/.qmx` default is gone. Its host probe opens the store directly, so the new refusal does not trip it.
  
  ## Every way it could lose, change, double or hide his data, and what closes it
  
  - **A copy that stops halfway.** The unfinished marker is written before the first copy. The host, the Library and a rerun all refuse it. The pointer is written only at the end. Proven by `test_a_corrupted_copy...` and lane 5.
  - **A copy that fills the disk.** There is an up-front room check (`test_too_little_room...`). A disk-full error in the middle leaves the folder marked unfinished, with the reason.
  - **A file changing while it is copied.** Each file is hashed as it is copied, the old folder is listed again, and every copy is rehashed. Proven by `test_a_file_that_changes...` and `test_a_corrupted_copy...`.
  - **An old folder that is a junction.** It is read through the link, and the report says so (`test_an_old_folder_that_is_a_link...`). The overlap check compares real paths.
  - **Links inside the old folder.** They are never followed, so the `claude-relayed/projects` junction does not double his chats.
  - **An old folder under a sync client.** It is read only. Cloud-only placeholders are refused, because reading them would download them into it.
  - **Two first starts at once.** The per-user lock refuses the second (`test_two_first_starts...`). The host lock on the new `data/` stops a host starting during the copy.
  - **An old folder LF2's rules refuse.** The same gate is used (`test_old_folders_lf2_refuses...`).
  - **A rerun after a finished bring-in.** It returns the saved report and copies nothing (`test_a_rerun...`).
  - **Copying into a second folder, which would double his data.** Refused (`test_the_same_old_folder_is_never_brought_into_a_second_folder`).
  - **Old-layout test junk.** The switch filters the 16 junk ids by id, and the report names them.
  - **Files left out are never hidden.** The old lock file, the old process record and every link are each listed with a reason.
  - **A host still running on the old folder.** Refused (`test_an_old_folder_a_host_still_serves...`).
  - **Rows still in `library.db`'s `-wal`.** They come through: the test fixture holds rows only in the `-wal`. The copy folds the WAL in before the switch, so the retired read-only copy is complete.

##### USER (sent while the lead was working) 2026-10-27T04:34
By the way, out of curiosity, isn't what we built yesterday just a graph? Well, I mean, the library and everything else combined, isn't just making a graph. Even what you see in the UI, isn't proposing a graph. Curious.

##### ASSISTANT 2026-10-27T04:35
Yes, mostly. That's a fair way to see it.

**The Library is a graph.** Every item is a node, and items connect through named links:

- "produced by" (this result came from that run)
- "uses" (this pod uses these bots)
- "variant of" (this version branched from that one)
- "tests" (this result tests that idea)
- "mentions" (this chat attached that report)

Each kind of item even declares its pages as walks along those links. A unit's "Logic" tab follows "uses" outward, "Results" follows "produced by" inward, and "Family tree" follows "variant of" both ways. The design's "Used in" map on an item is the same graph, drawn.

**The rest joins onto that graph:**

- A workflow is a graph of steps.
- A run links to the workflow it ran, the place it ran on, and everything it made.
- A chat links to what it attached.
- After yesterday, places are nodes too, so "where did this run" is one more link.

**What it isn't** is a graph database. Underneath, the Library is a versioned object store on SQLite: every item has versions, like git, and an edge table holds the links. The engine's run ledger is a separate event log. It's a graph in its shape, not in its storage. I think that's the right call: you get the graph's power (follow any link, draw any map) without running a second database, and every link is versioned and checked like everything else.

**What that buys you:** any "show me everything connected to X" question is a walk along links that already exist. "Which runs touched this dataset" or "what would break if I retire this bot" become walks, not new features.

  MD1 is pushed and its PR is open and ready. No probe disproved a design fact. One pre-existing gap turned up in lane 6, described under Findings.
  
  PR: https://github.com/MubarakHimself/QMX/pull/216 (base build/lf4, head build/md1, not a draft).
  Head: aced8cabc65487940916de8cc5c3326d736a442e (read with `git rev-parse HEAD`).
  `git diff --shortstat 4dd2c5c6`: 57 files changed, 1606 insertions(+), 510 deletions(-).
  
  ## What it does
  
  His digest, clippings and lineage now land in the Library he sees. Before, they went to a hidden fake file.
  
  - **Reads.** A script never opens the Library. `Served` in `E/nodes/script.py` answers the reads a node declares in `parameters.library_reads` onto its stdin under `library`. The verbs are `moved_to_main_after`, `find_by_intent`, `last_seq` and `published`, answered through the host's port while the host's Store stays open.
  - **Writes.** A script lists writes under `library` in its output. Each write is a body file under `library/` in the overlay, never inline bytes. At node finish the runner writes them on `refs/runs/<run_id>` as `run:<run_id>`, whatever the write claims.
    - Each artifact carries `metadata.write_key = <run:node:iteration:partition>:<index>`, and a write whose key is already on the run's ref is skipped.
    - Intent keys are prefixed with the workflow item.
    - Links must start from a handle of the same step, never use `produced-by`, `run-of` or `tested-by`, and point to an object that exists.

  ## Principles that shaped decisions
  
  - **Type System Discipline.** `library` is a required keyword on the service and the door, so a missing Library is a static error at every caller. Pyright shows 0 errors in the four packages.

  - **Model the Domain.** Reads are a verb table (`READS`), writes are two ops with uniform receipts, and the cursor's store is part of its key.

  Head, read with `git rev-parse HEAD`: 8c691031c499d5c3ff15e37e0103b4b71b81e032. Pushed, and the worktree is clean.
  Diff against build/md3: 14 files changed, 1622 insertions(+), 241 deletions(-).
  Commits: cc8eb35e (jobs, process_record, the folder refusal's kind, the switch's on_item) and 8c691031 (bring-in job, card, handover, exit codes).
  
  No probe disproved a design fact. One thing the plan left open is now partly checked. On this PC, the card's `first-start --serve` exits 0 and its last stdout line is the handover. Whether `serve` can bind the same port right after the card exits is still unproven, and lane 4 checks it.
  
  ### What it does
  - **Bring-in as a job.** `POST /api/first-start/bring-in` takes `first-start.lock`, runs the fast refusals and answers 409 at once, or 202 with a job. `GET /api/first-start/jobs/{id}` returns `{id, kind, state, step, done, total, progress, line, result}`. `progress` holds files_hashed/total, files_copied, bytes_copied/total and versions_switched/total. `GET /api/first-start` carries `job`, `unfinished`, `refused` and `warning`.
  - **Concurrent starts.** Two POSTs at once give one 202 and one 409 naming the job. A choice of new or open while a bring-in runs answers 409. So does a lock held by another process, with or without APPDATA; without it the lock is `qmx-first-start.lock` in the temp folder.
  - **Errors before the copy.** An OSError before the marker stops the job with one line, the long-path prefix removed, and leaves no marker.
  - **Start facts and `again`.** Start facts (`finished: false`) are written beside the unfinished marker. `again` clears only QMX's own copy. It needs the marker, saved facts that name the same old folder, and an old folder that still matches its list. Outside `data/` it removes only copies whose sha256 matches the old file.
  - **Long paths.** `long_path` is used by copy_file (opens, stat, utime), sha256_of, listing, _walk, _survey, the mkdirs and _room's exists() walk.
  - **Report counts.** The report counts old roots, not versions, both in the report and in `recheck_at_start`.
  - **Card choices and warnings.** A refused folder gets only "open". An unfinished folder gets bring-in again, open and restore, never new. The removable-drive warning shows on the default folder and on each choice's answer.
  - **Handover.** It answers the card's own last finished choice. It answers 409 before any choice, while a bring-in runs, after an unfinished one, and when an older pointer names another folder.
  - **Card exit codes.** `first-start --serve` binds once and exits 4 on a taken port, then exits 0 with the handover line last, or 1 if no folder was handed over.
  - **Host exit codes.** `serve`, `start`, `status` and `stop` exit 3 when a first start is due and 2 for a refused folder or an unswitched library.db.
  - **New modules.** `HO/jobs.py` and `HO/process_record.py`.
  
  ### Fast checks (by exit code)
  - Unit suites with `-n 2`. qmx-host: 115 passed, exit 0. qmx-library: 99 passed, exit 0. qmx-home: the first run had 1 failure, the departure below. After the fix, test_entry_points.py has 17 passed. Logs are `evidence/ls1/owner-unit-*.log`.
  - The changed test files after the last edit: 36 passed.
  - fmt-check, lint and types in qmx-host, qmx-home and qmx-library: all 0, with 0 pyright errors.
  - `tools/secret_scan.py`: exit 0, clean, after both commits.
  - Blast radius. The one fact is that the handover answer reaches the client before `server.run()` returns. I got it to step 4. `tests/test_handover.py::test_the_handover_answer_reaches_the_client_before_the_card_stops` serves the real app with uvicorn on a bound socket, gets the 200 answer, then sees the server thread end. The probe `evidence/ls1/owner-handover-probe.log` ran the real CLI card as a child process:
    - a handover before any choice answered 409;
    - a second card on the same port exited 4 with the port named;
    - after new, the handover answered 200, the card exited 0, and its last stdout line matched `{"handover": {"folder": ..., "port": ...}}`.
  - Other risks I cleared:
    - `host.STATE` is still re-exported, and test_templates_route asserts it.
    - No caller branches on the host's old exit 2: console.py only checks `!= 0`.
    - zones.py's `NoQmxFolder(line)` keeps kind refused.
    - The CLI bring-in now also locks when there is no APPDATA.
  
  ### Perf
  The probe was a 2,000-item synthetic folder, 3 interleaved rounds per side (`evidence/ls1/owner-perf-2000.log`). The parent side was the parent's own qmx_host source (`git archive 629bea16`) put ahead of head on PYTHONPATH, with head qmx-home and qmx-library under it.
  
  | Side | Median | Runs | Against parent |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Parent CLI | 112.16 s | 157.1, 112.2, 110.5 | baseline |
  | Head CLI | 115.10 s | 115.1, 120.8, 107.5 | +2.6 % (rule is 5 %) |
  | Head job | 102.17 s | 102.2, 111.6, 96.4 | -8.9 % |
  
  - **Job reads:** median 17.0 ms over 303 reads, max 97.3 ms (budget 50 ms). The mid-copy reload found the job all 3 times.
  - **What the numbers mean (inferred).** The Library switch's import, about 50 ms per item, sets the total. That matches LF4's 92.7 s. The 2.6 % sits inside the run-to-run spread of about ±7 %, and parent round 1 was a cold first run. The job is faster because it skips a Python process start.
  - **Measurement limits.** This is not a clean parent worktree, and 3 rounds is a small sample. The coordinator's own perf lane should confirm.
  
  ### Lane script
  `D:/QMX-worktrees/qma-ship/wrapup/evidence/ls1/owner-lanes.py`. It refuses any `--folder` that is not a new folder under `D:/QMX-worktrees/qma-ship/wrapup/homes/`; I tested it with C:/Temp/nope and it exited 2. It sets a scratch profile, unsets QMX_HOME, ANTHROPIC_*, CLAUDE* and NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA, and builds the old folder with `old_home` from the checkout's tests. Run it with the check copy's Python:
  - Lane 1: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -q -n 2` in qmx-agents/packages/{qmx-host,qmx-home,qmx-library}, at parent and at head.
  - Lane 2: `<check>/qmx-agents/.venv/Scripts/python.exe owner-lanes.py lane2 --folder D:/QMX-worktrees/qma-ship/wrapup/homes/ls-p1-job --checkout <check>` (2,000 items by default).
  - Lane 3: `... lane3 --folder .../homes/ls-p1-longpath --checkout <check>`.
  - Lane 4: `... lane4 --folder .../homes/ls-p1-handover --checkout <check>`. It runs lane 2, posts the handover, checks exit 0 and the last stdout line, then starts the host in this process on the same port with an in-memory keyring, Hindsight off and no browser, and checks /api/health within START_S.
  - Perf: `... perf --folder .../homes/ls-p1-perf --checkout <head-check> --parent <parent-check> --items 2000 --rounds 3`.
  
  I ran lanes 2 and 3 once each on 30 items as a smoke test, and both passed. I did not run lane 4 because it starts a host. Lanes 5 to 10 are not scripted.
  
  ### Departures from the plan (all named in the PR body)
  1. `qmx-agents/packages/qmx-home/tests/test_entry_points.py` is outside the Files block. Its host row expected exit 2 with no folder, and the plan makes it 3.
  2. `NoQmxFolder` gains `folder` beside `kind`. offer() needs the path to offer the bring-in from old data the pointer names, and to name the refused folder.
  3. The route answers 409 at once for a plain bring-in into an unfinished folder, and for `again: true` into a folder with no unfinished bring-in.
  4. The CLI `bring-in` gains `--again`, so the line the card prints for an unfinished folder names a command that works.
  5. The unfinished report's last line now offers the bring-in again instead of "Remove it and run the first start again".
  6. `first_start_router` and `first_start_app` take a required keyword `port`. `bring_in_old` takes `lock`, `progress` and `anew`.
  
  There is no QMB, QMF or QMN edit. Nothing touched his profile, browser or Credential Manager, and pg0 and Hindsight were never started.
  
  ### Findings (the harness refuses .md writes, so they are here as text)
  - **Backlog (LS1).** `qmx_control.library.old_library`, outside my Files, still tells him "Remove this QMX folder and run the first start again". `serve` prints that line when it exits 3 on an unfinished folder, while the card offers bring-in again.
  - **Backlog (LS1).** The card's drive rows still list only fixed drives. The warning is shown on the default folder and on each choice instead, which is the review F6 path.
  - **Low (LS1).** I could not make the 300-character test fail first on this PC, because LongPathsEnabled is 0x1. The helper's literal assertion in the same test fails first instead.
  - **Low (LS1).** Commit cc8eb35e on its own fails test_entry_points: the exit-3 expectation lands before the `__main__` change in 8c691031. The head passes.
  - **Low (LS1).** During `again`'s recheck of the old folder the step is "listing your old folder", but the counts do not move.
  - **Low (LS1).** A generic job error line uses `str(error)`, so a KeyError reads "it stopped with an error: 'x'".
  - **Low (LS1).** `again` leaves any `backups/pre-*` copies that a stopped run's store check made. They are harmless QMX copies.
  - **Idea (LS1).** The P5 install job can reuse `Jobs.start(kind, work, alone=True)` and `Stopped(line, result)` without editing jobs.py.

##### ASSISTANT 2026-10-27T13:01
Yes, about a thousand, and that's only the six parts this change touches. A test is a tiny automatic check, like "if the bring-in is killed halfway, does the old folder stay untouched?" They run in about 15 minutes with no one watching.

Roughly what each set covers:

- **Engine, 669:** running workflows (retries, triggers, crashes and resumes, saving results). Each of the roughly 40 templates also gets an install test.
- **Library, about 100:** saving, versions, search, and archiving test data out of sight.
- **Host, 121:** starting QMX, the first-start screen, bringing in your old data, and the handover.
- **Folder, 92:** finding your QMX folder and refusing wrong folders, which covers all those folder-move rounds.
- **Control, 151:** settings, keys and the server setup scripts.
- **Memory, 14.**

The whole project has far more. The backtesting engine alone has over 5,600.

Why so many: every bug we find and fix gets its own test, so it can never quietly come back. All those "it could move your Documents folder" rounds left tests behind, and those now check that rule on every change. That's what lets builders change things fast without breaking what already works.

Carrying on with wave 2.

  - **What happens:** `oauth.py:169` reads the endpoint's `errorCode` before it looks at the HTTP status. So `_renewed` (service.py:290-304) treats a 503 with `{"errorCode":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"}` as a revoked grant: it deletes the stored pair and says the sign-in ended. My probe on fakes showed exactly that: writes `[('delete', None)]` and `sign_in_ended`.
  - **Why it matters:** that pair is most likely still good. This breaks the builder's own claim that "a 5xx or unreachable answer never deletes", and the plan's rule that only a revoked grant is deleted.
  - **Fix:** in `_token_call`, treat any status of 500 or more as `bad_token_answer` before reading `errorCode`, and add a 503-with-errorCode test that asserts no writes and code `network`.
  
  **Lows (9):**
  - **L1:** the endpoint's `errorCode` text goes into the `sign_in_ended` line unfiltered (service.py:302). A misconfigured `[ctrader] token_url` that echoes its query would put the client secret and refresh token in the agent's line; my probe confirmed it.
  - **L2 to L5:** a few failures read with the wrong reason, and two narrow overwrite races exist outside the refresh lock. None of them stores a live grant.
  - **L6 to L9:** missing tests (the harness wiring, the case where accounts cannot be checked after a refresh), a stale broker README, and gaps in the evidence (lane 2's parent half, lane 10, a perf run by the coordinator).

  - **Secrets in any line or message:** none from QMX's own text. The only gap is L1.
  - **Two refreshing processes:** they converge, shown by the unit race test and the two-process lane.
  - **Trading scope:** the refresh never asks for it.
  - **Shipped set vs Spotware's:** the bytes are identical to the parent fixture (sha256 044991dd…3eb2), whose recorded source is Spotware tag 91. The test guards against drift but does not re-derive the bytes from Spotware.
  - **Refusal codes:** every failure inside a read maps to a closed code, so no raw exception reaches the agent.

  ### What changed for the operator and the UI agent
  
  - **The POST answers at once.** `POST /api/templates/install` used to hold one request until every template finished. It now answers 202 with a job view. The median was 34 ms across 3 runs, against 73 to 113 s at the parent.
  - **The job can be read while it runs.** `GET /api/templates/install/{job_id}` gives:
    - `step`, which names the template it is on, such as `installing morning-digest`;
    - `done` of `total`;
    - `result.rows`, with each finished row in the same shape the route answered before.
  - **The CLI no longer crashes on the new answer.** `python -m qmx_engine templates install` posts, then reads the job every 0.2 s and prints the same rows as before.
    - It still accepts an older host's list answer (review E22).
    - It installs in its own process only when its first POST cannot connect.
    - If the host is lost after it answered, the CLI prints "the host stopped during the install; start it and run the install again", exits 1 and starts no second install (F22). Lost means no answer, a restarted host that answers 404 for the job, or nothing listening.
    - A stopped job prints its rows, then `stopped: <line>`, and exits 1.
  - **Refusals.**
    - An unknown id gets a 404 by name, and no job starts.
    - A second install while one runs gets a 409 that names the running job.
    - A failed test run is a `test failed` row in a `finished` job.
    - A hop that raises one of the route's `FAILURES` ends the job `stopped`. Its line names the template, and its result holds `code` plus the rows finished so far (E21).
  - **For the next maintainer.** `templates_router(engine)` keeps its signature, so `HO/host.py` is untouched (E23), and `HO/jobs.py` is untouched too.
    - Each template is one `install_one` hop on the engine's loop in an empty context.
    - The router keeps each job's rows, appended only by that job's own thread, and the running view cuts them to `done`.

  Blocker 1 (lane 4, your question 1): a ledger file that is not SQLite breaks the done line on the real engine path. The cause is in qmx-engine/src/qmx_engine/ledger/store.py:272-274. `Ledger._run` runs `PRAGMA synchronous = FULL` before `migrate()`, and that pragma raises the raw `SQLITE_NOTADB` error before `open_sqlite` can turn it into `StoreRefused`. I checked on the check copy: the pragma raises `DatabaseError`, and `migrate()` alone raises the named `StoreRefused`. `serve_forever` already turns that into one line and exit 2.
  - Through the CLI, `check_open` refuses the file first, so only the late path is open.
  - It still blocks, because lane 4 is in the proving set and exit 1 sends the desktop app to the "host already runs" row.
  - The unit tests missed it because they patch `serve`.
  - **Fix:** in `E/ledger/store.py` `_run`, call `migrate(opened)` before the pragma, and add one engine test that opens a `Ledger` on a non-SQLite file and expects `StoreRefused`. This is a departure from the Files block.
  - The swap loses no durability: SQLite's default `synchronous` on this build is already 2.
  - Don't catch `sqlite3.DatabaseError` in `serve_forever`.
  
  Lane 7 (question 2): this is a script bug, and `start` is right. The stock `start` runs `check_open` in its own process, prints the line, and exits 2 through `parser.exit` before any child exists, so no host.log is written. owner-lanes.py:261 reads host.log without checking that it exists.
  
  The departures are all accepted: the two test edits, the last-line echo, the host's own started line, and the patched `serve`.
  
  Hardest questions:
  - **Bearer or path in the 503:** no bearer can appear. At most the body shows a market-store path inside his own folder, behind the bearer.
  - **Bind before open:** it does not change who wins on one folder, because the lock is still taken first.
  - **SO_REUSEADDR off Windows:** it cannot take a port that is listening. There is a bound-but-not-listening window on Linux (low 2).
  - **Start reporting success for a failed child:** no, apart from one same-folder race the parent also has.
  
  6 lows.

  - **Lock refusal (F1):** `qmx_home/files.py` raises `Busy`, and the bring-in's `Refused` subclasses it, so every existing catch still works and the card still answers 409.
  - **Secrets (F2, F3):** these files are left out of every copy and carried over on a same-folder restore: `data/vault/**`, `data/rclone.conf`, both Claude homes' `.credentials.json` and `.claude.json`, and `keys/`.
  - **What B7 seals:** `keys/vault.key`, the three `data/vault/` key files and `data/rclone.conf`. It never seals `tokens.json` (ruling 135), the Claude logins, `control-token` or a lock.
  - **Evictable blobs (F4):** `blobs/fetched`, `blobs/transient`, `cache/prices` and `queue/telemetry` are left out of copies. The files written once are `objects`, born blobs and tombstones.
  - **Finish never races a host (F5):** `finish` takes `restore.lock`, then `backups.lock`, then refuses on a live recorded host or a held `engine.lock`. The host's `single_instance` takes `restore.lock` first without waiting, so a second start refuses with one line. A failed rename changes nothing and `serve` exits 2.
  - **What a restore replaces (E-M1):** a separate check route answers the counts (runs, Library ref moves, chats, price months). The restore itself needs `confirmed: true`, or `--yes` on the command. I chose this over a one-route preview so a client that never shows the counts cannot restore.
  - **Start after a restore (E-M2, E-S3):** one pause covers both. No replicator is built, and the engine's own `autonomy.paused` is set. One carry-on resumes both, giving at most one catch-up fire per trigger. The copy's interrupted runs are listed before he presses it.
  - **Restore into a new folder (E-M3):** the folder is made with `resolve(create=True)` and marked `restore-unfinished.txt`. The pointer is written only after the finish. The card offers the restore again, and `serve` exits 3.
  - **Sweep (E-M4):** every manifest ends with a trailer line. A torn manifest is never thinned, and while one exists the pool sweep does not run.
  - **Keep rule (E-M5):** counts are of the newest buckets that hold a copy, not windows back from the clock. The newest copy and the newest copy that passed a drill are always kept. Thinning runs only after the new manifest is in place.
  - **Quick undo after a purge (E-M6):** a missing file that has a tombstone is skipped. A purged blob is purged again at the first start, so its ref moves too.
  - **Quick undo room (E-M7):** it refuses below the larger of 1 GiB and the host's floor. The doctor row shows its size.
  - **Second drive (E-M8):** it is only a proposal until he accepts it through `POST /api/backups/targets/default/accept`. Nothing is written outside the QMX folder before that.
  - **Newer-format folder (E-M9):** the manifest header carries the label's `format_version`, `min_reader` and `last_written_by`, plus each SQLite file's own versions. The finish writes them back into the label.
  - **Another folder's copy (E-S8):** it goes through only with an explicit `replace`, since his data is set aside either way.
  - **Damaged pool file (E-S9):** the drill deletes it, and the next round pools it again. No mark file is added.
  - **Quick copies from before an earlier restore (E-S14):** they read their files from the set-aside folder of the first restore after them.
  - **Keys outside the vault's allow-list (E-S11):** the sealed copy uses exactly `is_replicable`'s list. The passphrase route names `qmx/firecrawl`, `qmx/tool/*` and the two `qmx/ctrader-client-*` entries as left out, so he knows to type them again.
  - **Wave overlap:** B2 now adds every `restore.py` reader B5 calls, and B5 owns the `single_instance` change, so wave 3 shares no file.

The reviewer found two real problems in the first backup PR, so I've sent it back to the builder for its one fix round.

- **After an interrupted backup, QMX refused its own drive.** If the backup process was stopped partway (PC shut down, process killed), the next backup would refuse the drive. It wrongly thought another QMX folder had used it, and it stayed stuck until you clicked "carry on".
- **A power cut could plant a bad file that every later backup trusts.** To save time, the builder stopped forcing each copied file onto the disk. A power cut or a pulled USB drive mid-backup could leave a damaged file that later backups reuse without checking. I've told the builder that keeping your files safe comes before speed. If that pushes it past the speed limit, I'll set a new one rather than accept the risk.

The builder is also fixing three smaller gaps in the same round:
- A backup that couldn't read a file still counted as complete, so an old complete copy could have been deleted in its place.
- One damaged file stopped every backup to your second drive.
- A target inside your QMX folder could slip through when reached by a shortcut-style link.

When the fix lands, I'll rerun the checks and a reviewer will check the fixes. Nothing is merged.

##### ASSISTANT 2026-10-27T22:27
The reviewer found two serious problems in the restore PR, and I've sent it back for its fix round:
- **The drill could delete any file on your PC.** The drill is the regular test that a copy restores. A copy's file list was trusted as written. A list edited by hand on a plugged-in drive could point the drill at any file on your PC, and the drill would delete it. The fix only accepts real file fingerprints, so nothing outside the backup folder can ever be touched.
- **A deleted file could come back.** If you permanently deleted something, such as a secret, while a restore was waiting for the next start, the restore would put it back. The fix removes such files again when the restore finishes.

The builder is also fixing four smaller gaps that could leave a restore stuck or half-checked. The full checks are still running in the background. Nothing is merged.

  **Ideas:**
  - A "back up now to every place" round needs `run_round` to take a set of places.
  - The doctor row and view call `proposal()`, which walks `data/` (cached an hour). The first call can take seconds on a large folder.
  
  **Lows in my own work:**
  - My lanes measured "within two minutes" from the moment the host served, not from its spawn. Host start was about 15 s, so 61.7 s from serve is 77 s from spawn.
  - The health test takes about 20 s.
  
  **Principles that shaped choices.**
  - Model the Domain: a `Standing` per place, read from the log, decides concern and readiness, instead of booleans spread across the sweep.
  - Make Operations Idempotent: incidents are reconciled by signature from the log, so a restart or a repeat never recounts them.
  - Boundary Discipline: `Backups` raises a domain `Refusal`, and only the router turns it into HTTP.
  - Test Behavior: tests use literal lines and incident counts, and the health test runs against a real socket.
  - Laziness Protocol: I imported two round helpers rather than duplicating them or editing B1's file.
  - Prove It Works: lane 2 found the wrong doctor row name, `backup`. I fixed it to `backups` and pinned it with a test.

The only brake is that a copy refuses if it would leave D: with less than about 2.9 GB free (a twentieth of the free space when QMX starts); the quick undo has no size limit of its own.

  - Two gaps break your rule that every setting must be editable from the screen. The hourly copy on this PC is fixed in the code, so you can't change it or switch it off. And the screen can't show you some settings, such as how many copies are kept, so it would show blanks.
- **Disk space:**
  - Copies don't duplicate your whole folder. Each file is stored once, and unchanged files are skipped.
  - Your big files that never change, like Library items and finished price months, are never copied into the hourly copy.
  - A database that changed is copied whole each time. With a few GB of QMX, the hourly copies could grow to roughly 3 to 11 GB on D:.
  - The only brake is that a copy stops if D: would drop below about 3 GB free.
  - If you named C: yourself as a place, nothing would stop it filling C:.
- **Your server:** it can't hold copies with what's built. Only folders on a drive work today. The server or an R2 bucket needs PR 6, which isn't built yet.
- **Overlap:** two older pieces partly overlap, the weekly GitHub snapshot and the mini-app backups. The mini-app one should be merged in when PR 6 is built. Nothing else overlaps.
- **QMN, QMF and the "open" tool:** the tool you remember is OpenObserve. Its data can be rebuilt from what the Library already keeps, so it needs no backup. The trading node wasn't touched. One QMF file was touched: saving prices now waits up to about 1.3 seconds if a backup is reading that file. That was never measured with a big price file.
- **Number of PRs:** the four built PRs are big enough to justify being separate. The last three could have been two, so five PRs in total would have done.

##### ASSISTANT 2026-10-28T17:03
You're describing one pattern, and it's a good one. **Save the recipe, not the cake.**

**1. Save the settings, not the outputs.** n8n, OpenCode and Claude Code all work this way: a whole system is a few hundred lines of JSON, and the program rebuilds everything else from it. QMX is already mostly built like that. Each workflow is a folder with a definition file, each mini app has a manifest, settings are one settings file, and units will be lean by design. So what needs saving is small:
- the recipes (workflows, mini-app manifests, units, settings);
- your own content (Library items you made, chats, memory);
- the run results that matter, because AI answers don't come out the same twice.

Everything else gets rebuilt from those.

**2. Zip.** Yes. Text compresses five to ten times. Each file carries a fingerprint, so a corrupted zip is caught on the spot, never trusted. Your "re-zip from scratch once a month, then check it" idea is ordinary maintenance. QMX already has scheduled workflows, so that maintenance can be a monthly workflow, with an agent attached if you want.

**3. Search indexes.** Like the index at the back of a book. QMX builds them so search is fast, and can always rebuild them from the content. No need to save them.

**4. rclone.** It's one program that talks to about 70 storage services: Google Drive, Cloudflare R2, Contabo, your server and more. A friend connects their own Google Drive and it just works. Spreading data across several of your accounts is possible too: rclone has a mode that treats several drives as one. I'd test that before promising it. And note that Google may not like pooled free accounts.

**5. Back up before every update.** That's standard, and QMX half-does it already. Before an update changes a database, it copies that database first. Your version is better: sync everything to your account first, then update.

**6. OpenObserve across machines.** It's partly done. Local-first added one setting for every machine: send nothing (the default), send to this PC, or send to a named server. The server already has OpenObserve installed. Not verified yet: whether picking "this PC" sets OpenObserve up on your laptop by itself, and whether it's running on the server right now.

Compared with Grafana and Prometheus: that route is three or four programs to install and wire together. OpenObserve is one program that holds logs, metrics and traces, with its own web page. For one person, the simpler one is right, and I'd keep it.

**What I'd pick, without growing anything:**
1. **Tonight:** fix or park PR 229. Then the first real start once you've landed the 22 PRs.
2. **Tonight, writing only:** a one-page design for "sync to your account". It covers what gets saved, the one switch, the storage you connect, zip plus a monthly re-zip, and sync before update. No code yet.
3. **Tonight, writing only:** update the UI agent's notes with the backup and sync settings and the missing "Deep logs" switch.
4. **Tonight, reading only:** check whether OpenObserve really works on more than one machine, so I don't guess.
5. **After launch:** build the sync design as one or two PRs, not seven.

Tell me what you find on OpenObserve, and whether this list is right.

  Findings that most change the design:
  
  1. **Save recipes, fetch the rest, and leave per-machine settings out.** Chrome syncs an extension as its id, version and update URL. VS Code skips settings marked "machine". n8n saves credentials as id, name and type only. OpenCode refers to secrets as `{env:}` / `{file:}`.
  2. **Products don't merge on their own; they show both copies.** Steam and VS Code let the person pick. Android restores app data before the first launch. For QMX, the only thing that can clash is the "latest copy" pointer, so a restore should show both latest copies.
  3. **Packs beat zip.** I measured QMX's 701 template files (1.35 MB) myself:
     - each file compressed alone: 2.4x smaller;
     - zip: 2.0x;
     - each file alone with a trained zstd dictionary: 4.8x;
     - one zstd stream over everything: 5.9x.
  
     Google Drive moves about 2 files per second, so loose files are slow. The restic/kopia ideas to copy are a hash→pack index, prune past 5% unused, checking one slice each month, and one machine that owns maintenance.
  4. **Don't use rclone `union` for the pool.** From reading its source (not tested): if one member fails to open, the whole union fails, and a member that fails while listing drops out silently. R2 cannot report free space, so it can't join a free-space rule. QMX should treat each account as its own place and choose placement itself. Use `copy` only; `bisync` isn't needed.
  5. **QMX needs its own Google sign-in client.** rclone's shared Google Drive client "will stop working during 2026". The QMX client should be a published Desktop app using `drive.file`; one left in "Testing" loses its sign-in every 7 days.
  6. **The step-by-step dialog already exists in rclone.** `rclone config create --non-interactive` returns each question as JSON.
  7. **Keep free space on any Google account that holds his email.** Over quota, Gmail "can be impacted", and after 2 years the content may be removed.
  8. **Correction to 02-inventory:** Google's terms don't say outright that using several accounts for storage is abuse; the risk is still there.
  9. **OpenObserve has a Windows build, but three defaults must change.** It keeps data 10 years, sends telemetry, and lets its disk cache take 50% of free disk. Its MCP server is in the free edition, but every tool there runs with full rights, delete included. Self-hosted Enterprise is free up to 50 GB a day and adds read-only roles for agents.
  
  Not verified: union, bisync and config create were not run against a real account, and whether OpenObserve runs without Administrator is untested.

Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  PR https://github.com/MubarakHimself/QMX/pull/233. build/sy3 is pushed at f00e3f67 (read with `git rev-parse HEAD`). It holds two commits on top of 59ff776d: 88abdf01 adds the tests, and f00e3f67 is the fix.
  
  **Cause.** The coordinator's guess was only half right. I traced every failure in 50 loaded runs at 59ff776d, and 8 of them failed. In 3 of the 4 I traced fully, the prune's second read of the copies did see the new copy. But the second fix protected only packs being deleted, so a pack that same prune let go took the copy's only file out of the index. In the fourth run, the copy landed 6 ms after the prune's last read. The data is in the census logs: the second read returned True for 3 runs, and in the fourth the read was at 88.420 and the manifest at 88.426. No prune-side read can see a copy written after it, so the second fix's premise could not hold.
  
  **Fix** (repository.py and round.py only).
  - After writing its copy, a send reads the storage's lists again. If a file the copy names has no named pack, it takes the copy down, sends the file again and rewrites the copy. After 4 checks it reports the send stopped and leaves no copy.
  - A pack on the drop list is never trusted or named again. Before deleting one, the prune writes each file a copy still needs into a new pack.
  - A prune keeps a pack it was letting go if a copy written during that prune needs it.
  - A let-go now counts from the moment the pack went on the drop list. The drop line stays until the delete.
  - A restore reads a file still in a let-go pack from that pack's own list.
  
  **Proof.**
  - Both new tests fail at 59ff776d and pass at the head: the slow-writer order, and a copy written while a prune runs.
  - test_the_one_fact passed 30 of 30, unchanged. 10 runs used `-n 4` beside a full qmx-home suite, and 20 ran ten at a time. The re-pack deleted 40 to 98 packs per run.
  - Lane 4 ran twice and passed both times. It deleted 20 and then 8 packs, and every copy restores.
  - Fast checks: qmx-home 347 passed and qmx-host backups 28 passed. fmt-check, lint, types and secret_scan all exit 0.
  
  **Still open (logged in findings-lows).** One case is not closed. A send can stall longer than the window between its last check and writing its copy. If it is then killed at the next check's first step, the copy can still name a deleted file.
  
  **Mishap, fixed.** A cleanup glob deleted my saved copy of the PR body, so one edit briefly left only the new section. I rebuilt the full body from GitHub's edit history, and all six sections are back.
